name: Sheba son of Bichri
charge: Insurrection: we have no part in David
summary: On the heels of Absalom's rebellion, Sheba the Benjamite blew a trumpet and cried, every man to his tents, O Israel, and all Israel went up after him. David judged him more dangerous than Absalom. He was besieged in Abel of Beth-maachah.
offense: The return of David was followed by strife between the men of Judah and the men of Israel over their share in bringing the king back (2 Samuel 19:41-43). Into that contention Sheba the son of Bichri blew a trumpet and declared that Israel had no part in David or inheritance in the son of Jesse. The men of Israel went up after him, while Judah clave to the king (2 Samuel 20:1-2). The rebellion drew strength from a quarrel that should not have governed the people's allegiance. Sheba offered separation as the answer to wounded tribal honour. The kingdom had scarcely emerged from Absalom's conspiracy when another man turned contention into a summons to depart. David saw that Sheba could do greater hurt if he gained fenced cities. The pursuit brought Joab's army to Abel of Beth-maachah, where it raised a bank and battered the wall (2 Samuel 20:6, 14-15). One man's cause now placed a whole city's life and inheritance beneath the danger of a siege.
judgment: A wise woman called to Joab from the city and asked why he would swallow up the inheritance of the Lord. She identified herself with those who were peaceable and faithful in Israel (2 Samuel 20:16-19). Her appeal distinguished the city's people from the rebellion of the man within it. Joab answered that he did not seek to destroy the city. Sheba had lifted his hand against David; if the city delivered him alone, the army would depart (2 Samuel 20:20-21). The demand narrowed the matter to the rebel instead of treating everyone behind the wall as equally guilty.

entries.commentary: A man of Belial, a devil, named Sheba the son of Bichri, blew a trumpet and cried that they had no part in David nor inheritance in the son of Jesse, and every man of Israel went up from David to follow Sheba, while the men of Judah clave unto the king from Jordan to Jerusalem. David came to his house in Jerusalem and took the ten concubines Absalom had defiled, put them in ward, and fed them but went not in unto them; they were shut up in widowhood until the day of their death because Absalom had gone in unto them.

David told Amasa to assemble the men of Judah within three days, but Amasa tarried longer than the set time. So David sent Abishai with Joab's men, the Cherethites, the Pelethites, and all the mighty men to pursue Sheba lest he escape into fenced cities. At the great stone in Gibeon, Joab came to Amasa with a sword secretly fastened, took him by the beard with his right hand as if to kiss him, and smote him in the fifth rib so that his bowels shed to the ground, and he died at one stroke. Joab was grimy and shady, murdering the man who had been named captain in his place. One of Joab's men stood by Amasa calling all who favored Joab and David to follow after Joab. Amasa wallowed in his blood in the midst of the highway, and when the people stood still to look, the man removed him into the field and cast a cloth over him, and then all the people went on after Joab to pursue Sheba.

Joab pursued Sheba through all the tribes to Abel of Beth-maachah, and they cast up a bank against the city and battered the wall to throw it down. A wise woman of the city called out to Joab, reminding him of the old saying that men would surely ask counsel at Abel, and asked why he would swallow up a city that was a mother in Israel and the inheritance of the Lord. Joab answered that he did not seek to destroy, but only wanted Sheba the son of Bichri, who had lifted up his hand against the king; deliver him and he would depart. The woman promised that Sheba's head would be thrown over the wall. She went to all the people in her wisdom, and they cut off Sheba's head and cast it out to Joab, who blew the trumpet and retired from the city, every man to his tent, and returned to Jerusalem unto the king.

Joab was over all the host of Israel, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada over the Cherethites and the Pelethites. Adoram was over the tribute, Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was recorder, and Sheva was scribe. Zadok and Abiathar were the priests, and Ira the Jairite was a chief ruler about David. Do not read merely to say you read four chapters; read and truly study to give the sense and understand the scriptures. --- Topics: [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

Thou shalt not sacrifice unto the Most High any bullock or sheep wherein is blemish, or any evilfavouredness, for that is an abomination unto the Lord thy God. Back then you could be put to death for sacrificing a bullock or sheep with a blemish, because doing an abominable thing carried death.

If there be found among you man or woman that hath wrought wickedness, transgressed the covenant, and gone and served other gods, the sun or moon or any of the host of heaven, which the Most High commanded not, the matter had to be established first. A lot of people do not know how to apply [Leviticus 5:1](/bible/leviticus/5#v1); the precept for [Leviticus 5:1](/bible/leviticus/5#v1) is [Deuteronomy 17:4](/bible/deuteronomy/17#v4). Whether it be told thee or thou hast heard of it, thou shalt enquire diligently, and behold, if it be true and the thing certain that such abomination is wrought in Israel, then judgment proceeds. Make sure you are certain of a thing before you bring somebody to judgment; only after diligent enquiry was the man or woman brought to the gates and stoned with stones till they die.

At the mouth of two witnesses or three witnesses shall he that is worthy of death be put to death; at the mouth of one witness he shall not be put to death. The hands of the witnesses shall be first upon him to put him to death, and afterward the hands of all the people. Wait till we go back to this: the ones who witnessed against you were the first to lay hands on you, so a false witness could not hide behind the crowd. So thou shalt put the evil away from among you.

If there arise a matter too hard for thee in judgment, between blood and blood, between plea and plea, and between stroke and stroke, matters of controversy within thy gates, then thou shalt get thee up into the place which the Lord shall choose. Come unto the priests the Levites and unto the judge that shall be in those days, and they shall shew thee the sentence of judgment; thou shalt do according to all that they inform thee, according to the sentence of the law which they shall teach thee, declining neither to the right hand nor to the left. The man that will do presumptuously and will not hearken unto the priest that standeth to minister before the Most High, or unto the judge, even that man shall die; and all the people shall hear, and fear, and do no more presumptuously.

When thou art come unto the land and shalt say, I will set a king over me like as all the nations that are about me, thou shalt in any wise set him king whom the Lord thy God shall choose: one from among thy brethren; thou mayest not set a stranger over thee, which is not thy brother. These are the laws for a king that is to rule over Israel. He shall not multiply horses to himself, nor cause the people to return to Egypt to multiply horses, for the Lord hath said, Ye shall henceforth return no more that way. Neither shall he multiply wives to himself, that his heart turn not away. You hear a lot of these dudes today saying king this and king that, and many of the same men pushing for multiple wives; the law of the king says do not multiply wives to thyself. Neither shall he greatly multiply to himself silver and gold.

When he sitteth upon the throne of his kingdom, he shall write him a copy of this law in a book out of that which is before the priests the Levites. It shall be with him, and he shall read therein all the days of his life, that he may learn to fear the Most High and keep all the words of this law and these statutes to do them. The purpose: that his heart be not lifted up above his brethren, that he turn not aside from the commandment to the right hand or to the left, and that he prolong his days in his kingdom, he and his children, in the midst of Israel.

verses.text: And there happened to be there a man of Belial, whose name was Sheba, the son of Bichri, a Benjamite: and he blew a trumpet, and said, We have no part in David, neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse: every man to his tents, O Israel.
So every man of Israel went up from after David, and followed Sheba the son of Bichri: but the men of Judah clave unto their king, from Jordan even to Jerusalem.
And David said to Abishai, Now shall Sheba the son of Bichri do us more harm than did Absalom: take thou thy lord’s servants, and pursue after him, lest he get him fenced cities, and escape us.
And he went through all the tribes of Israel unto Abel, and to Beth–maachah, and all the Berites: and they were gathered together, and went also after him.

And they came and besieged him in Abel of Beth–maachah, and they cast up a bank against the city, and it stood in the trench: and all the people that were with Joab battered the wall, to throw it down.
Then cried a wise woman out of the city, Hear, hear; say, I pray you, unto Joab, Come near hither, that I may speak with thee.
And when he was come near unto her, the woman said, Art thou Joab? And he answered, I am he. Then she said unto him, Hear the words of thine handmaid. And he answered, I do hear.
Then she spake, saying, They were wont to speak in old time, saying, They shall surely ask counsel at Abel: and so they ended the matter.
I am one of them that are peaceable and faithful in Israel: thou seekest to destroy a city and a mother in Israel: why wilt thou swallow up the inheritance of the Lord?
And Joab answered and said, Far be it, far be it from me, that I should swallow up or destroy.

The matter is not so: but a man of mount Ephraim, Sheba the son of Bichri by name, hath lifted up his hand against the king, even against David: deliver him only, and I will depart from the city. And the woman said unto Joab, Behold, his head shall be thrown to thee over the wall.

Then the woman went unto all the people in her wisdom. And they cut off the head of Sheba the son of Bichri, and cast it out to Joab. And he blew a trumpet, and they retired from the city, every man to his tent. And Joab returned to Jerusalem unto the king.

And the man that will do presumptuously, and will not hearken unto the priest that standeth to minister there before the Lord thy God, or unto the judge, even that man shall die: and thou shalt put away the evil from Israel.
